rationale.text: The glossary entry on controlling the consultation of a media lists the mandatory functions, and the methodology repeats them. They must all be present, so each is a requirement: play with pause or stop, always; a sound toggle when the media has sound; a captions toggle when it has captions that are not burned in; an audio description toggle when it has an audio description. The last three apply only when their condition holds, which the entry records as exceptions. None of this can be decided by code. Whether a media has sound, separate captions or an audio description is known only by playing it. Which elements of a custom player perform which function is not marked in the code, and the native controls of audio and video elements are drawn by the browser, with buttons that vary by browser and by media. Even a video element without the controls attribute is not a mechanical fault: a custom player may provide every function, and the wording limits the test to media that need controls (si nécessaire), which is judgment, for instance for a decorative background video. No axe rule is tagged for this test and no check is registered, so there are no links and the entry stays at none. Applicability is judgment: whether an element is a temporal media cannot be decided with certainty, and the glossary counts media played through svg, canvas or a plugin. Needs lists media, to know whether the media has sound, captions or an audio description, and state, because player controls often appear only on hover or focus.
